ordered_diagnoses: Factor VII deficiency with skin necrosis

s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of skin necrosis with respiratory failure and bacteremia
salient_findings: Erythema and edematous necrotic plaques of the bilateral ears
Necrosis progressed to involve earlobe and helix
Biopsy showed full-thickness necrosis with sparse inflammation and adnexal epithelia necrosis
key_facts: Patient has a medical history of factor VII deficiency hemophilia
Presented with acute hypoxic respiratory failure
Intubated with prone positioning
Developed Staphylococcus hemolyticus bacteremia
Erythema and edematous necrotic plaques appeared on bilateral ears
No devices were used on the ears
Necrosis progressed over time
Biopsy showed detached epidermis with full-thickness necrosis
Biopsy showed necrosis of adnexal epithelia, including folliculosebaceous units and eccrine glands

shortlist.why_kept: Acute onset of skin necrosis with respiratory failure and bacteremia, consistent with purpura fulminans

shortlist.label: Warfarin-induced skin necrosis

shortlist.why_kept: Presence of bacteremia and respiratory failure, which can trigger DIC, and skin necrosis is a possible manifestation

shortlist.label: Factor VII deficiency with skin necrosis

raw.rationale: The patient's condition, including the development of erythema and edematous necrotic plaques on the ears without any device usage, along with full-thickness necrosis and necrosis of adnexal epithelia, is consistent with warfarin-induced skin necrosis, especially given the context of a coagulopathy like factor VII deficiency hemophilia which may have been exacerbated or complicated by anticoagulant therapy

rejected.label: Purpura fulminans
rejected.why: While purpura fulminans can cause skin necrosis, it is typically associated with severe infections and disseminated intravascular coagulation, and the biopsy findings here do not specifically suggest this diagnosis

rejected.label: Disseminated intravascular coagulation
rejected.why: DIC can cause skin manifestations but the specific pattern of necrosis and the biopsy findings do not directly point to DIC as the primary cause

rejected.label: Necrotizing fasciitis
rejected.why: Necrotizing fasciitis involves deeper tissue destruction and typically requires surgical intervention, which is not indicated in the provided information

rejected.label: Factor VII deficiency with skin necrosis
rejected.why: While the patient has factor VII deficiency, the specific skin manifestations described are more characteristic of warfarin-induced skin necrosis, suggesting an iatrogenic component rather than a direct result of the factor VII deficiency
